summary: Phase F of Partner API v1 (webhooks HMAC+retries hardening, IP allowlist, per-partner feature-flag overrides, admin partner management, per-partner rate-limit override, partner suspension, security headers, Developer Portal WEB) is fully green — 26/26 pytest cases PASS + all web UI flows verified. Backend: (Webhooks) GET /webhooks/events returns the expanded catalog including sponsored_game.created / conversion.recorded / reward_event.recorded / job.completed / merchant.created / offer.created / ping — verified. POST /webhooks creates a webhook with chosen events + returns a whsec_ secret. Firing POST /conversions produces an async delivery to example.com — a delivery row is CREATED (delivery_id + event_type=conversion.recorded + ok=false + status_code=405 as expected because example.com rejects POST). GET /webhooks/{id}/deliveries lists it. POST /webhooks/{id}/rotate-secret returns a NEW whsec_ that differs from the original. POST /webhooks/{id}/deliveries/{delivery_id}/retry replays it (returns delivered:false because example.com still 405s — the endpoint itself returns 200); unknown delivery -> 404 delivery_not_found; unknown webhook rotate -> 404 webhook_not_found. HMAC signature is added by _deliver via X-RadioLife-Signature=t=<ts>,v1=<sha256>. (IP Allowlist) Minted a THROWAWAY sandbox key under prt_Ngu4e33qm4KULA + set ip_allowlist=['203.0.113.5'] via services.partner_api.set_key_ip_allowlist. Call to /api/v1/me with that key returns 403 {error:{code:'ip_not_allowed'}} — confirmed. Full-scope key (no allowlist) continues to work. Throwaway key revoked in teardown. (Feature Flags) POST /api/admin/partner-api/partners/{id}/flags {flags:{iter125_probe:true, audio_preroll:false}} accepted; GET returns the same; GET /api/v1/capabilities exposes overrides in feature_flag_overrides and merges them into feature_flags — verified iter125_probe=true + audio_preroll=false. Cleanup POST flags={} succeeds, capabilities.feature_flag_overrides no longer contains the probe key. (Admin Partner Mgmt) GET /partners lists shared partner; GET /partners/{id}/credentials returns dict; GET /partners/{id}/usage?days=30 returns 200; POST /partners/{id}/status with invalid value 'banana' -> 400 invalid_status; POST /partners/{id}/rate-limit {per_minute:900} -> 200 rate_limit_per_minute=900; POST /partners/{id}/keys/key_missing/revoke -> 404. (Suspension) POST /partners/{id}/status {status:'suspended'} -> subsequent calls with the shared key eventually 403 {error:{code:'partner_suspended'}} — enforcement went effective within a few seconds (well below the ~60s cache bound). Reactivated + cache-cleared + verified /me returns 200 again — SHARED KEY LEFT WORKING. (Security Headers) X-Content-Type-Options=nosniff, Referrer-Policy=no-referrer, Cache-Control=no-store are stamped on 200s, 401s, and 404s — plus the existing X-RadioLife-API-Version:1 + X-Request-ID. (Regression A-E) 20+ endpoints re-smoked, all 200. FRONTEND (web /advertiser/dashboard/api): page loads with testid developer-api-page. All Phase-F sections render (dev-keys-section, dev-oauth-section, dev-usage-section, dev-webhooks-section, dev-explorer-section). Create API key -> dev-secret-reveal shows the secret in a <code> block once (65-char rlk_test_... verified). Create webhook with selected event chips (conversion.recorded + reward_event.recorded) -> webhook whk_... visible; rotate-secret click surfaces a new whsec_; delete webhook works (Webhook removed toast). API Explorer: paste the freshly-minted key into dev-explorer-key, default endpoint /capabilities, click dev-explorer-send -> dev-explorer-response shows HTTP 200 + full JSON body including feature_flags/environment/api_versions. IP allowlist input + save (dev-key-ip-input-<id> / dev-key-ip-save-<id>) is wired. All test-created data cleaned up.

minor.issue: list_deliveries hard-caps at limit=20 with no cursor pagination — deliveries beyond the last 20 are silently unreachable via the API. Portal path routes/partner_portal.py:207 also uses the same 20-item cap. Add cursor pagination consistent with /reward-events + /conversions + /jobs.

Requires scope 'campaigns:write' rather than a new 'webhooks:write' scope (kept for backward-compat per E1 note). If a partner subscribes to webhooks WITHOUT ever booking campaigns, they still need campaigns:write to rotate — misleading scope model. Consider introducing webhooks:read/write and accepting either during the deprecation window.

Retry backoff is a fixed 0.5*(attempt+1) with only 3 tries in a single request — a transient blip (e.g. 502) beyond ~1.5s is not eventually consistent because there's no queued retry outside the initial delivery. Manual /retry works but there's no auto-retry after the first burst.

Deliveries are fired via `asyncio.create_task` without a global concurrency bound. A burst of conversions to a partner with N webhooks fans out to N*3 concurrent httpx clients — no rate-limiting. Consider a bounded semaphore.

ui_bugs.issue: When rotating a webhook signing secret, the new whsec_ is surfaced in dev-secret-reveal but the SAME testid is used for both API-key reveal AND webhook-secret reveal — a user can't visually distinguish 'this is a webhook secret vs an API key' unless they read the label text. Consider separate testids like dev-webhook-secret-reveal-<id>.

The UI omits the 'ping' event chip while the /webhooks/events catalog includes it. This is intentional (ping is a synthetic test event) but the label text 'Events (none = all)' is misleading — if a user selects none, backend defaults to WEBHOOK_EVENTS INCLUDING ping, so the partner may receive ping events unexpectedly. Add a UI note that 'ping' is only for /ping tests OR exclude 'ping' from the default fan-out in services.partner_api.create_webhook.

issues: Hydration warning in console: '<span> cannot be a child of <option>' — an EnvBadge or similar span is being rendered inside a <select><option> in the AdvertiserSidebar/env picker. Not blocking but pollutes the console. See React hydration warning in browser console.

action_items: (minor/pagination) Add cursor pagination to /webhooks/{id}/deliveries + portal deliveries endpoint (both hard-cap at 20).
(minor/scope) Introduce webhooks:read + webhooks:write scopes; keep campaigns:read/write during a deprecation window. Update /webhooks POST + rotate-secret + deliveries + retry to accept either.
(minor/robustness) Bound emit_event fan-out with a semaphore + persist failed deliveries into a retry queue so a partner with a transient outage eventually receives events.
(minor/UI) Split dev-secret-reveal into distinct testids for API-key vs webhook-secret reveals so testing agents + users can tell them apart.
(minor/UI) Fix hydration warning: <span> is rendered inside <select><option> somewhere in the advertiser sidebar (visible on /advertiser/dashboard/api).

(minor/product) The default webhook subscription (no events specified) subscribes to ALL events including 'ping'. Either drop 'ping' from the default set in create_webhook or hide 'ping' behind an explicit opt-in.
critical_code_review_comments: services/partner_api.py::_deliver stores `event` (the FULL delivered payload) in every deliveries row (line 603). That's necessary for /retry, but for a high-volume partner (thousands of events/minute) the partner_webhook_deliveries collection will bloat quickly. Consider a TTL index on partner_webhook_deliveries.ts (e.g. 30 days) or move event payloads to a separate keyed store.

services/partner_api.py::rotate_webhook_secret updates the secret in-place with no grace window (line 640). Any in-flight delivery signed with the OLD secret will fail verification on the partner side. Standard pattern is to accept both old + new for ~24h. Add `previous_secret` + `previous_secret_until` fields.

services/partner_api.py::_partner_meta caches (limit, active) for 60s (line 447). set_partner_status + set_partner_flags pop the cache but ONLY on the same process — in a multi-worker/multi-pod deploy, a suspend will take up to 60s to propagate to other workers because there's no cross-process cache invalidation. Acceptable for now but call it out in ops runbook.

routes/partner_api_v1.py::_usage_mw sets Cache-Control via `response.headers.setdefault('Cache-Control', 'no-store')` (line 66). If a downstream endpoint explicitly sets Cache-Control (e.g. for public caching of /capabilities), the security-hardening `no-store` will be silently overridden. Consider force-overwriting to `no-store` on error responses at minimum.

services/partner_api.py::_client_ip + _ip_allowed — the resolver picks caller IP from X-Forwarded-For/X-Real-IP with no strict trust boundary. In a Kubernetes ingress deploy this is fine because the ingress rewrites XFF, but a partner could spoof X-Forwarded-For if the app were run directly. Document trust boundary or pin to a specific trusted-proxy IP list.

routes/partner_portal.py::admin_partner_status returns 200 immediately after set_partner_status even though the enforcement cache is only invalidated locally. Any admin script that suspends then immediately hits /api/v1 will see the OLD state for up to 60s. Consider surfacing 'effective_at' in the response.

The frontend DeveloperApi.jsx does not display the webhook signing secret persistently (correct, security), but there's no 'copy the secret to clipboard' step in the rotate flow — a user who dismisses the reveal will have permanently lost their secret and must rotate AGAIN. Consider showing a 15-second countdown OR forcing an 'I've saved it' click before dismissal is allowed.
